answer: Admission is tied to one numbered cold-press at a headland mill. The applicant collects a sealed sack of tagged walnut kernels from a single lot and may start that press only when an unannounced dawn bell rings. The fresh cake must then dry on that press's outdoor lee rack while a catalogued gale crosses the mill's weather mast. Registrars match kernel lot, press stamp, cake moisture curve, and the mast tape. A shared press, a restuffed sack, or an oven-dried cake is forfeited. Fielding N aliases costs N exclusive presses, N unique lots, and N live watches from first light through the storm.
